items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Basie motioned for Frank Wess and Frank Foster to come forward. Wess played flute and Foster tenor on the two numbers I did with the band

ctx.x: alright. Ten o'clock that night there was no Les McCann and he didn't show until intermission. He was supposed to play before Basie, and I was to do my bit after he and his trio. He offered no excuse for not being there at 10, but I tried to get with him regardless. I asked him if we played "Tea for two" would that be alright with him? He said he didn't know it. I asked him if he knew "Sweet Georgia Brown" or "Caravan" and he told me he didn't. After that answer, I knew he was a liar and had not wanted to…

I started talking with Budd Johnson who was one of the tenor men with Basie and told him the Les McCann story. He wasn't Les McCann for me anymore but Les My Can.. Bud suggested that I ask Basie if he would allow his rhythm section to play with me and said that Frank Wess, the other tenor man could accompany me on piano. Then Budd said that he personally would put the proposition to Basie which he did. Bill (Basie) was very understanding about the deal and thought that My Can had played a dirty trick on me, which…

And when Basie introduced me the reception I received was the greatest I ever had in my career and I was so thrilled that when I spoke in the mike I offered to pay a drink for everyone there. If the public had really taken me at my word, it would have taken me a year to work out the debt to pay for all those drinks because there were at least 3000 people there.
